summary: H.R. 9678, titled the "Good Jobs for Good Airports Act," requires employers of certain airport service workers at small, medium, and large hub airports to pay prevailing wages and provide fringe benefits. It establishes enforcement mechanisms for the Departments of Labor and Transportation, mandates monthly employer certifications under penalty of perjury, and allows interested persons to bring civil enforcement actions.

affected_groups.effect: Receive guaranteed minimum hourly wages and fringe benefits based on the higher of federal Service Contract Act rates or local/state rates, with protections regarding loading, passenger assistance, security, ticketing, ground-handling, cleaning, concessions, and catering.

Must pay mandated prevailing wages and fringe benefits, submit monthly certifications under penalty of perjury, face investigations and record examinations, and risk civil penalties or civil lawsuits for non-compliance.

Tasked with issuing wage determinations, establishing regulations, conducting investigations, receiving monthly certifications, publishing complaint data, and enforcing the new labor and certification standards.
affected_groups.group: Secretary of Labor and Secretary of Transportation

key_provisions: Requires covered employers at small, medium, and large hub airports to pay covered service workers at least the higher of the Service Contract Act prevailing wage or applicable state/local minimum wages.
Requires covered employers to provide fringe benefits matching or exceeding Service Contract Act determinations or applicable state/local laws.
Mandates that covered employers submit monthly certifications under penalty of perjury to the Secretary of Transportation confirming compliance with wage and benefit rules.
Directs the Secretary of Labor to issue initial wage and fringe benefit determinations within 120 days of enactment using Service Contract Act methodologies.
Grants the Secretary of Labor investigative and enforcement powers under the Fair Labor Standards Act, and grants the Secretary of Transportation authority over employer certifications.
Establishes maximum civil penalties for violations of up to three times standard civil penalties and permits interested persons to bring civil enforcement actions in U.S. district courts.
missing_information: Specific dollar amounts for the prevailing wages or fringe benefits that will be determined by the Secretary of Labor.
The exact baseline operational costs for employers or federal agencies to implement and oversee the certification and reporting requirements.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 9678, titled the "Good Jobs for Good Airports Act," requires employers of certain airport service workers at small, medium, and large hub airports to pay prevailing wages and provide fringe benefits. It establishes enforcement mechanisms for the Departments of Labor and Transportation, mandates monthly employer certifications under penalty of perjury, and allows interested persons to bring civil enforcement actions.
summary_detail.significance: This bill establishes uniform federal wage and benefit floors tied to the Service Contract Act for a broad category of airport service workers across small, medium, and large hub airports. It creates new administrative reporting duties, oversight authorities for multiple federal departments, and expanded legal liabilities for employers.
